articles.title: Who's to blame for Washington's season-defining blunder?
articles.summary: The Commanders blunder Sunday was an all-timer, and there is plenty of blame to go around.
articles.body:
Every NFL season brings a few moments that defy explanation. The quarterback who throws a 50-yard bomb through a hole somehow smaller than a football. The wide receiver who slips the bonds of gravity. The running back who shrugs off a full ton of defenders. And, of course, the team that commits an error so egregious, so unthinkable, that the entire fan base is left wondering why these guys aren't fired on the spot.

Sunday brought us the usual assortment of thrilling games and odd endings, but there was no game which ended in a more inexplicable smash-your-TV fashion than Washington's utter flop against the New York Giants . After 69 minutes and 46 seconds of vintage NFC East football, and still with the chance to win the game on a field goal in overtime, the Commanders instead melted like cotton candy in the rain:

This isn't 4D chess here; the correct play should have been to spike the ball and kick a 41-yard field goal. Instead, the Commanders ran some kind of messy short-yardage play that went nowhere, ending with everyone sort of casually milling about at walkthrough speed until someone realized that, hey, this game is seconds away from being over. And by then, it was far too late, and the Commanders came away with a tie when a victory was right there for the taking.

How did they manage to botch the kind of play that ought to be automatic? Who's to blame here? Let's line up the suspects:

The buck always stops with the head coach, full stop. Quinn accepted the blame for the utter mismanagement, saying after the game that he should have had Daniels simply spike the ball. Plus, on a broader scale, the fact that the players seemingly weren't prepared for this kind of critical contingency falls squarely on Quinn's shoulders. After Washington's spectacular 2024, he and the Commanders have nose-dived, and this game punched through to a new level of futility.

Daniels has a lot to answer for, from not throwing the ball out of bounds to not running his team with necessary urgency in the waning seconds to allowing himself to get sacked. His postgame explanations were less than convincing; he has to be more locked in than he showed in those final seconds on Sunday.

Blough calls the plays for Washington, while Quinn handles the in-game decisions. Still, the fact that the play was run at all — instead of just opting to spike the ball — is the most damning part of the sideline decision-making. When you've lost the support of effervescent minority owner Magic Johnson, you've truly lost everything:

Sure, they were just following the play that was called, but running 15-plus yards downfield helped slow down the team's return to the line of scrimmage.

Moved with all the urgency of teenagers asked to go clean their rooms. The exception: right tackle Josh Conerly Jr., who you can see in the above clip trying to get Daniels to, you know, hustle it up and get to the line .

"Accidentally" kicked the ball while ambling back over to his position as the referee attempted to spot it. A-plus gamesmanship right there.

They did absolutely nothing wrong, but Washington fans should try blaming them anyway, to take the heat off their own team's atrocious mismanagement.

A win would have changed the entire calculus of the season for Washington; the Commanders at 2-3 would have been in a three-way tie for second in the NFC East. (It's OK to laugh at that.) But now they have to wear the shame of this lost opportunity for the rest of the week, right up until next Sunday, when they … play 5-0 San Francisco in prime time.

Yeah, it's going to get worse before it gets better for Washington. Soon enough, there'll be more than enough blame to go around.

articles.title: B/R's Week 6 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: We're heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and fantasy managers face a range of outlooks based on their records.
articles.body:
We're heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and fantasy managers face a range of outlooks based on their records.

For those at 4-1, everything is coming up roses. At 3-2, there's room for improvement, but they're still on the right side of .500.

Conversely, a 2-3 start isn't ideal, but it's more manageable than 1-4, especially for managers dealing with injuries and disappointing production.

Regardless of their circumstances, all fantasy managers have one thing in common: They want a win in Week 6. We want to help you do just that with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to this week's player rankings (which include the top 124 players overall to assist in making "flex" lineup calls), a few quick notes.

The first is the same as always—the overall rankings do not include quarterbacks. If your league employs a "superflex" spot and you have a viable QB2, start them there. Even mediocre signal-callers are generally more consistent as flex options.

The second is that Week 6 is the first four-team bye week—the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings are all off. This may be the only week that Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs doesn't blow up.

Finally, if you're sitting at 1-4 and in last place, the last thing you want from this writer is a pep talk. Believe me, I know your pain. But don't look at the hole you're in as one big problem. Break it down into smaller ones. Treat every week like a mini-season all its own. Make some waiver-wire moves, and don't be afraid to be bold with your lineup decisions.

Find a way to eke out a win in Week 6 and then try to stack a few victories.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is one of one.

For most quarterbacks, completing just 12 passes and throwing just a single touchdown pass would portend at best a mediocre fantasy week. But Allen is not most quarterbacks—despite just 210 passing yards against the Los Angeles Rams, Allen also ran for 121 yards and another touchdown on the way to finishing third in fantasy points among quarterbacks for the week.

Allen now has eight rushing scores for the season and is the highest-scoring quarterback by a wide margin.

Paying up for him this year may not have been such a bad idea after all.

Josh Allen wasn't the only quarterback who piled up rushing yards in Week 5—in his return from a dislocated elbow, Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders ran for 103 yards and a pair of scores against the New York Giants.

Drake Maye of the New England Patriots started the season slowly—Maye failed to amass 10 fantasy points in any of his first three starts. But Maye has been on fire the past two weeks—including 374 passing yards, four touchdown passes and a rushing score last week against the Las Vegas Raiders.

There's some optimism that Lamar Jackson (ankle) of the Baltimore Ravens will be able to return in Week 6—so much so that he's included in this week's rankings. But Tyler Huntley played well in Jackson's stead—if the Ravens play it safe and sit Jackson another week Huntley would check in as a decent QB2 against the Cleveland Browns.

Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (vs. Washington Commanders)

Purdy has gone from a low-end fantasy QB1 in drafts over the summer to the highest-scoring fantasy quarterback in the NFC. The good times will keep rolling on Monday night against Washington's 29th-ranked pass defense.

Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys (at Green Bay Packers)

Many fantasy managers will have little recourse but to roll Prescott out Sunday night against the Packers. But Prescott has quietly had just one 20-point game this season and draws a bottom-five fantasy matchup for the position at Lambeau Field.

Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Cousins has quietly been a top-10 fantasy quarterback over the first five weeks of the season, and he could have another solid outing in Week 6. The Bills are doing many things well right now, but playing defense is not one of them.

The Pittsburgh Steelers opened the season with a committee backfield, but while Rico Dowdle (toe) has been sidelined, Jaylen Warren has done his level best to establish himself as the team's lead back.

Warren has been nothing short of outstanding the past few weeks. After piling up 181 total yards and two touchdowns last week against the Indianapolis Colts, he has averaged 107 rushing yards a game over that span, adding just over 40 yards per contest over that same stretch.

Warren is fourth in PPR points among running backs over the last three weeks, and head coach Mike McCarthy has called him " the man " in the Pittsburgh backfield.

Injuries continued to mount in the backfield in Week 5. David Montgomery of the Houston Texans (groin) and TreVeyon Henderson of the New England Patriots (ankle) both left their games early. Quinshon Judkins of the Cleveland Browns (ankle) finished the loss to the New York Jets, but he was spotted in a walking boot after the game.

The Philadelphia Eagles may have to hold running back tryouts in the parking lot of The Linc—with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and backup Will Shipley (foot) both expected to miss Week 6, Dameon Pierce has rapidly gone from the practice squad to Philly's lead back.

Entering the season, Omarion Hampton of the Los Angeles Chargers was viewed as a rising talent and fringe RB1. But the Bolts have struggled, and Hampton is sharing work in a three-headed backfield. He ranks as RB36 in PPR scoring through five weeks.

Emanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks (at Denver Broncos)

Wilson has scored on the ground each of the last two weeks, although he also fumbled in both of those games. The fourth-year veteran will make it three games in a row with a touchdown this week against a surprisingly porous Denver defense.

Woody Marks, Houston Texans (at Jacksonville Jaguars, London)

With David Montgomery on the shelf, Marks will be a popular player on waiver wires this week. But he should be benched where possible in Week 6—the Jaguars led the league in run defense last year and are right back in that spot in 2026.

Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Pierce was not great last week in London, gaining just 14 yards on 11 carries. The sledding should be significantly easier this week against the Panthers, who have surrendered 156.5 yards per game on the ground in 2026.

The Los Angeles Rams came up just short Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. But wide receiver Puka Nacua can't be blamed for the setback that dropped the Rams to 2-3 for the season.

Nacua has missed time this season, but when he's been out there, he has been productive, culminating in a ridiculous 17/138/1 stat line against the Bills.

Nacua is averaging just over eight yards per catch this season—not very Nacua-like—but he was Week 5's highest-scoring wideout. He's averaging a jaw-dropping 15 targets per game, and only Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba is averaging more PPR points per game.

Nacua now looks poised for another big week against the Arizona Cardinals.

The list of banged-up wide receivers continues to grow. Although fantasy managers got Justin Jefferson back in Week 5, several other receivers suffered injuries.

Deebo Samuel Sr. of the San Francisco 49ers hurt his hamstring, CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys sustained a quad contusion, and Roman Wilson of the Pittsburgh Steelers is expected to miss time with a finger injury.

Among this year's high-scorers at wide receiver in fantasy leagues, the biggest early surprise may well be Christian Watson of the Green Bay Packers. Watson caught two long touchdown passes in last week's win over the rival Bears, and he's third at the position in PPR points after five weeks.

The trade last weekend that sent Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston has rekindled hopes that the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft can resurrect his lagging career. But now Harrison has to learn a new offense, and Nico Collins is the unquestioned alpha in that passing game. Harrison's still an end-of-the-bench fantasy reserve.

Luther Burden III, Chicago Bears (at Atlanta Falcons)

Burden's production has taken a hit with all the shakeups at quarterback in the Windy City. But if Caleb Williams can't play Sunday, Case Keenum should get the nod—and he frequently targeted Burden in his first start this year.

Ladd McConkey, Los Angeles Chargers (at Kansas City Chiefs)

McConkey's disastrous 2026 season continued in Week 5—he was active but didn't play a snap against the Broncos. Now he gets a Chiefs team allowing the fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts five weeks into the season.

Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Tucker has been relatively quiet since a big outing in Week 2, but if ever there was a week for him to have another huge game, this is it. The Buffalo pass defense is a sieve, and the Raiders are going to have to throw to keep up with the Bills offense.

That Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders sits fifth in fantasy points among tight ends might seem a little disappointing at first glance—until you realize he has only played three games.

Since missing the first two games of the season with a knee injury, Bowers has been highly productive. Even in last week's blowout loss to the New England Patriots, he caught eight of 10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown.

Bowers has topped 20 PPR points in all three of his starts this year, and his 23.7 PPR points per game is more than 5.5 points higher than Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals.

Tight ends haven't been hit by injuries as hard as wide receivers, but a couple of players at the position went down. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq of the New York Jets and T.J. Hockenson of the Minnesota Vikings both suffered concussions.

Minnesota's Week 6 bye gives Hockenson additional time to recover before the team's next game.

Isaiah Likely of the New York Giants was a trendy breakout pick in 2026, and through five weeks at least he deserves some credit. He was the highest-scoring tight end of Week 5 thanks to an 11/94/2 line, and he sits second at the position in PPR points for the season.

It may be time to start having uncomfortable conversations about Colston Loveland of the Chicago Bears. Last week in Titletown, Loveland had two catches for 19 yards, and he barely has more PPR points for the season than Bowers is averaging per game.

Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

After five catches for 83 yards last week against the Buffalo Bills, Higbee sits sixth in PPR points at tight end over the last three weeks. Meanwhile, the Cardinals have given up the fifth-most PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

Kyle Pitts, Atlanta Falcons (vs. Chicago Bears)

Pitts caught five passes for 42 yards and a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5. However, he faces a tougher fantasy matchup Sunday against a Bears team allowing the third-fewest PPR points to tight ends this season.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

With eight catches for 61 yards and three touchdowns over the last two weeks, it might be a stretch to call Freiermuth a "sleeper." His productive stretch could continue this week in a plus fantasy matchup for tight ends with the Buccaneers.

Kickers are changing late-game strategy across the NFL.

In just the past few weeks, we have seen a pair of games decided by kickers hitting a 57-yarder as time expired. Both teams had less than 10 seconds left when the ball was kicked off to them.

But a touchback followed by a 25-yard completion—or a long kickoff return—can put a team at the opponent's 40-yard line. A kicker like Jacksonville's Cam Little can bang it through from there with room to spare—with a defensive tackle snapping the ball, no less.

What used to be desperation kicks that only a couple of kickers in the league had a real chance to hit are now commonplace.

We are going to see a 70-yard field goal soon.

For the most part, the Houston Texans defense has disappointed to this point in the season. But edge-rusher Will Anderson Jr. can't be blamed for those struggles—after three sacks last week against the Tennessee Titans, Anderson has an NFL-high 7.5 sacks for the year.

It wasn't supposed to be this way, but the Los Angeles Chargers have become an offense to target with fantasy defenses, allowing the most fantasy points per game to the position in the AFC. With the Kansas City Chiefs coming off their bye and playing at home, they are an elite fantasy play in Week 6.

Five weeks in, five kickers have attempted at least 10 field goals without a miss: Spencer Shrader, Will Reichard, Evan McPherson, Jason Myers and Andre Szmyt.

New England Patriots Defense (vs. New York Jets)

After a rocky start to the season, the Patriots have rebounded in a big way the past two weeks, with the defense playing a big part. Over the last 15-plus years, the Jets have one win at Gillette Stadium. One.

Spencer Shrader, Indianapolis Colts (vs. Tennessee Titans)

Since Week 2, Shrader has peeled off four straight games with at least 12 fantasy points. Now, fantasy's highest-scoring kicker gets a Titans team allowing the most fantasy points per game to kickers this year.

Las Vegas Raiders Defense (vs. Buffalo Bills)

The run with the Raiders defense was fun while it lasted—but it's over. The Raiders have fallen out of the top-12 after back-to-back clunkers in bad matchups, and now Vegas hosts the buzzsaw that is the Buffalo Bills offense.

Tyler Bass, Buffalo Bills (at Las Vegas Raiders)

After his game-winning heroics on Monday night, Bass has climbed into the top 10 among fantasy kickers for the season. But the Raiders have been giving up far more extra points than field-goal attempts the past couple of weeks.

Baltimore Ravens Defense (at Cleveland Browns)

The Ravens haven't been especially relevant in fantasy—the team barely ranks inside the top 20 in fantasy points. But this week Baltimore draws a reeling Browns offense that just allowed eight sacks to the New York Jets.

Chris Boswell, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Boswell is one of this writer's favorite kickers—a steady veteran on a good (but not great) offense. Throw in a top-five fantasy matchup for his position with the Buccaneers this week, and you have the recipe for success.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Tom Brady missed four games over Deflategate 10 years ago, but the NFL’s controversial punishment still sparks debate
articles.summary: Tom Brady returned to the New England Patriots on October 9, 2016, after serving a four-game suspension over Deflategate, helping his team beat the
articles.body: Tom Brady returned to the New England Patriots on October 9, 2016, after serving a four-game suspension over Deflategate, helping his team beat the Cleveland Browns 33-13. A decade later, the punishment remains a source of disagreement among NFL fans, former players and sports commentators. The league accused Brady of being aware of the use of under-inflated footballs during the 2015 AFC Championship Game, an allegation he denied throughout the dispute. The case triggered a lengthy legal fight and cost the NFL millions of dollars, leaving a question that has never quite gone away: did Brady deserve to miss those four games?Tom Brady’s Deflategate suspension followed a lengthy legal battleThe controversy began after the Patriots beat the Indianapolis Colts in the AFC Championship Game in January 2015. An NFL investigation led by general counsel Jeff Pash and attorney Ted Wells examined whether New England personnel had deliberately deflated footballs.According to ESPN’s report on the investigation, the league concluded it was “‘more probable than not’ that Patriots personnel deliberately deflated footballs during the AFC Championship Game, and that Brady was probably ‘at least generally aware’ of the rules violation.”Brady received a four-game suspension without pay. A federal judge overturned the punishment in September 2015, offering him a temporary victory. The NFL successfully reinstated it in April 2016, however, and the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected Brady’s appeal that May.The quarterback consequently missed New England’s first four regular-season games in 2016. He returned against Cleveland in Week 5, throwing for 406 yards and three touchdowns in the Patriots’ comfortable win.The dispute had already stretched far beyond the football field. ESPN reported that the NFL spent roughly $22 million over two years investigating the allegations, pursuing legal action and disciplining the organization.Darrelle Revis and Brady’s father revealed the personal tollFor Brady, Deflategate was not simply a fight over equipment rules or a suspension. Darrelle Revis, his former teammate in New England, recalled seeing the quarterback struggle emotionally when he addressed the team.“When the Deflategate happened, and Tom was the headliner of the whole situation, he addressed us as a team. You can tell he was distraught,” Revis said on Apple TV+’s documentary The Dynasty.Revis said Brady directly rejected the allegations in front of his teammates.“He said, ‘This is something I wouldn’t do. I would not ruin the season for us. The allegations are false.’ He was actually bawling his eyes out in front of us.”Brady’s father, Tom Brady Sr., also described the strain the controversy placed on the family.“It was extraordinarily difficult in the life of the Brady family,” he said in the documentary. “Not only did I suffer from it, but my wife, it crushed her. Because he’s not a liar.”Those accounts offer a different perspective on a case often reduced to arguments about football pressure and competitive advantage. Brady’s supporters saw a player fighting a punishment he believed was unjust, with his reputation and family life caught in the fallout.Jason Kelce and Bob Costas questioned the NFL’s responseBrady himself later found humor in the league’s costly investigation. During his Netflix roast in May 2024, he took a swipe at the money spent pursuing the case.“If they had given me the $20 million, I would have just told them I f---ing did it,” Brady quipped.Former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce was more direct about his opposition to the punishment. Speaking on the New Heights podcast, he said, “I don’t even think Tom should have gotten in trouble for deflating footballs. I’m pro deflating footballs. I’ll say it. I’ll say it. I am pro deflating footballs.”Kelce continued, “He outsmarted people. Why the f--- does it matter how much air is in that motherf-----?”The former center added, “If you’re throwing it and catching it, who the f--- cares?”Veteran sportscaster Bob Costas also criticized the league’s handling of the scandal in 2015. He argued that officials had “overreacted” and “turned a misdemeanor into a federal case, both figuratively and literally.”Costas compared the situation to other forms of competitive gamesmanship, including watering down a playing field to slow an opponent or using pine tar on a bat. He acknowledged that Brady’s own response had contributed to the controversy, saying the league “perhaps overreacted and Brady himself didn’t say what he could’ve said.”Ten years on, Deflategate remains a revealing test of how the NFL handles discipline, evidence and public trust. Brady served the suspension, returned to win games and later won another Super Bowl with New England. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Top WR Targets After Marvin Harrison Jr. Dealt to Texans
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. may not be the last notable wide receiver to move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. may not be the last notable wide receiver to move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler cited multiple wideouts who could plausibly be dealt over the next few weeks.

The Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. is the first name Graziano mentioned because the 2024 first-round pick is going backwards for the second straight season. He has just nine receptions for 105 yards and one touchdown.

Fowler questioned whether the Jaguars would trade Thomas given their 4-1 start, and the NFL insider cited how Thomas' value goes a little beyond the raw stats.

"His immense skill set requires defensive backs to play him deep, which opens the field for Washington and Meyers," Fowler said. "But if Jacksonville gets a good offer, it would be foolish not to consider it."

He had a similar opinion on the Cleveland Browns' Jerry Jeudy, who has fallen behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the pecking order.

"The Browns are improved and need veteran help, so my sense is while they are not actively shopping Jeudy, a strong offer could change that," Fowler reported.

He went on to say that Los Angeles Chargers receiver Quentin Johnston "has come up in a few of my recent conversations."

The Chargers are 0-5, so they could wave the white flag and be a seller at the deadline before too long. Graziano spoke to one source who's skeptical L.A. has that much that other teams will want, though.

In the case of Johnston, his production (seven receptions and 108 yards) isn't very good, and he has a $16.5 million option for 2027. His market could be limited.

Fowler closed out the conversation by throwing the Baltimore Ravens' Rashod Bateman and Minnesota Vikings' Jauan Jennings into the mix.

In general, there are opportunities out there for teams in need of receiver help. However, all of the candidates on the board either carry some risk or are likely to have limited upside.

articles.title: Simone Biles reveals how her embarrassing skin condition journey inspired Arcutis Biotherapeutics awareness campaign
articles.summary: Talk about a warrior - on the spring floor as well as outside of it.
articles.body: Talk about a warrior - on the spring floor as well as outside of it. Olympic gymnast Simone Biles recently opened up about a personal health struggle that left her feeling self-conscious.But she thoughtfully turned her embarrassing experience with an inflammatory skin condition into an awareness campaign for Arcutis Biotherapeutics.Indianapolis Colts safety Jonathan Owens’ wife has partnered with the biopharmaceutical company for its “Skin to Believe In” campaign. The initiative encourages people living with eczema and seborrheic dermatitis to seek medical help and explore treatment options.The campaign was announced on September 29; it draws attention to skin conditions that cause persistent itching, flaking, and visible changes.According to Arcutis Biotherapeutics, nearly 36 million Americans suffer from inflammatory skin conditions like seborrheic dermatitis and the most common form of eczema - atopic dermatitis.Simone Biles, wife of Jonathan Owens, reveals eczema struggleIn a Healthline interview, Simone Biles revealed that she mistook itching and flaking on her scalp for dandruff. She even worried that the symptoms could be contagious. Beyond her scalp troubles, she also noticed recurring dry patches on her arms.These skin symptoms became frustrating, particularly during her gymnastic training. She would catch herself scratching on the uneven bars or balance beam while waiting her turn to come. She would scratch until she bled.She felt uncomfortable about how the flakes showed up on camera during photoshoots. She would try to conceal them with oils.The Olympic gold medalist had spent years experimenting with over-the-counter products. She tried several shampoos, creams, and oils. But nothing relieved her skin condition. Embarrassment and demanding training schedules delayed her from seeking professional help for her skin ailment.Biles finally revealed her skin sorrows on social media during the 2024 Paris Olympics. Immediately thereafter, she sought skin help from a dermatologist. She finally found a name for her condition. She was diagnosed with seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, while she had eczema [atopic dermatitis] on her arms.Zoryve treatment helps manage skin symptomsAfter she found a name for her unknown skin condition, Simone Biles finally embraced relief with Zoryve [roflumilast]. Arcutis Biotherapeutics developed this prescription topical medication - the 0.3% foam formulation relieved her seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, while the 0.15% cream helped her eczema on her arms.She praised the treatment, saying it easily fit into her busy routine. She found the medication non-greasy, easy-to-use, and stressed that it’s not a steroid, pill, injection, or shampoo. The timely treatment reduced Biles’ itching and flaking problem. The eczema patches on her arms also became clear.Caution note: individual effects can vary, so patients should consult a healthcare professional before starting treatment to determine appropriate options.Arcutis campaign aims to break skin condition stigmaSimone Biles collaborated with Arcutis Biotherapeutics for its “Skin to Believe in” campaign. The world-renowned gymnast hopes to help others overcome the embarrassment and misconceptions that come with visible skin conditions.Through her partnership, the Olympic gold medalist hopes people come forward and speak openly with healthcare providers about their skin troubles, instead of quietly enduring the symptoms or relying on home remedies.“I’ve learned that we can’t fix every problem on our own and it’s okay to seek help,” Biles said in the campaign announcement. This initiative clearly shows how her personal experience inspired Arcutis Biotherapeutics’ awareness campaign.Arcutis and Simone Biles connection explainedArcutis CEO Frank Watanabe said that Biles’ first encounter with Zoryve came organically and started on social media. The decorated gymnast shared her skin problems in a TikTok post during the 2024 Paris Olympics, the CEO said in an interview.Dermatologists recognized her itchy, flaky scalp symptoms as seborrheic dermatitis and encouraged her to explore available treatment options. They encouraged her to check out some of the FDA-approved products available for the condition.That’s how she got started on Zoryve and connected with Arcutis. “She’s a very enthusiastic supporter of the product. Working with her is great,” Watanabe said via Fierce Pharma.Arcutis has worked with other public figures to raise awareness of inflammatory skin conditions - professional golfer Max Homa and actress Tori Spelling, along with her daughter Stella McDermott, in its “Free to Be Me” patient awareness campaign for inflammatory skin conditions.Simone Biles’ stress management tricksHealthline contacted Simone Biles’ dermatologist, Angela Lamb, MD, who said that stress can contribute to eczema flares. Personalized care is essential because weather conditions and individual triggers can also flare symptoms.Beyond treatment, Jonathan Owens’ wife told Healthline that managing stress is a crucial part of health. She spends time with her friends, gets her nails done, enjoys a massage, and takes a bath at night to unwind herself.She also said that stepping away from her demanding gymnastics career helped her relieve her stress. “Honestly, without training every single day, I don’t feel as stressed.” Biles said. “[Everyone] can find different ways to alleviate their stress. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Carson Beck's Timeline to Become Cardinals QB1 Amid 1-4 Start to Season
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck reportedly may not get a chance to prove himself on the field until later in the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck reportedly may not get a chance to prove himself on the field until later in the 2026 season.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that although he "absolutely" expects Beck to get some playing time this season, sources have indicated that it may not happen until late November, which is when Arizona's schedule gets easier.

Over their next six games, the Cards are at the Los Angeles Rams, home for the Denver Broncos, at the Dallas Cowboys, at the Seattle Seahawks, home for the Rams and at the Kansas City Chiefs.

On Nov. 29, the Cardinals host the Washington Commanders, which could be a softer landing spot for the rookie third-round pick out of Miami.

Arizona also has a three-game stretch against the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders from Weeks 15 through 17, which would give Beck a chance for success.

The Cardinals are currently 1-4, although it wouldn't necessarily be fair to blame veteran starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett for that.

He has done a solid job given the obvious shortcomings of the team as a whole, completing 66.3 percent of his passes for 1,110 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions.

Fellow veteran Gardner Minshew II is actually still listed as Brissett's backup, but Graziano noted that Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made comments Monday that suggest Beck could soon leapfrog him.

Entering the season, it was widely assumed that Beck would get the chance to start a handful of games at some point unless the Cards shocked the football world and got into playoff contention with Brissett at the helm.

Since that appears unlikely, it makes all the sense in the world for Beck to play eventually.

The Cardinals are one of many teams that could be looking to select a quarterback early in the 2027 NFL draft, although the 24-year-old Beck flashing starter potential could possibly change their outlook.

On the flip side, if Beck plays and doesn't look good, Arizona would perhaps be even more convicted in pursuing a new franchise signal-caller.

The death of a father at Six Flags Over Georgia has raised serious questions about ride safety, even as the company prepares to report its next earnings results. The tragedy also comes at a difficult time for the amusement park operator, which has struggled to regain investor confidence. Travis Kelce, who has ties to Six Flags as an ambassador and investor, adds another layer of public interest to the company's latest setback.Six Flags shares fall after fatal Goliath roller coaster accidentSix Flags shares suffered a sharp decline on Tuesday, October 13, after a visitor died on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. The stock closed at $10.20, down around 14% for the day, while reports indicated an intraday decline of more than 16%. It marked the company's lowest closing price since 2009.The victim was identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old father and educator from the Atlanta area. He died on Monday after falling from Goliath, a 200-foot-tall roller coaster known for its high speeds and steep drops.According to local reports, Kariem was riding with his son while his wife and daughter watched from the ground. Witnesses described a horrifying scene as he fell from the ride. Authorities have not yet confirmed what caused the accident.The incident prompted Six Flags to temporarily close nine roller coasters across six parks while safety concerns were assessed. The company also expressed condolences to Kariem's family and said it was cooperating with local authorities investigating the death.“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. articles.title: Terry Bradshaw hints at retirement, says his time as an NFL analyst is 'coming to an end'
articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw has been a mainstay at Fox for over three decades.
articles.body:
One of the most well-known faces on NFL Sundays knows he's closing in on the end of his career. Long-time NFL analyst Terry Bradshaw hinted at retirement Tuesday, telling "NBC News Daily" he knows his "time on television as a sports broadcaster is coming to an end ."

Bradshaw, 78, appeared on the program discussing his new memoir, which is titled "Looking for Terry." During the interview, Bradshaw was asked about his busy schedule, which is when he said he was nearing the end of his broadcasting journey.

While Bradshaw did not reveal his retirement plans, he will be a significant loss whenever he decides to step away from his current role. After a Hall of Fame playing career — one that saw Bradshaw win four Super Bowls — the quarterback immediately signed a broadcasting deal with CBS in 1984. He was an in-game analyst with the network for years before eventually joining its pregame program in 1990.

Four years later, Bradshaw left the network for the same gig at Fox, where he's remained ever since. Over the years, Bradshaw has established himself as a staple of the network's pregame show "Fox NFL Sunday" where he appears in studio alongside Howie Long, Curt Menefee, Michael Strahan and many others.

While Bradshaw is known for his affable personality, his memoir — which was released Tuesday — focuses on his depression diagnosis, struggles with cancer and failed marriages. The broadcaster said that subject matter made his book a tough sell to publishers, who only wanted to hear stories about football.

For now, Bradshaw is still sharing those stories with fans every Sunday. While his retirement might not be imminent, the long-time analyst knows his on-camera time is approaching its end.

articles.title: President Trump was expected to attend Steelers-Bucs, before his schedule changed
articles.summary: The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game.
articles.body:
The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game. But it ultimately didn't.

On Tuesday, Kristen Holmes of CNN reported that President Trump was expected to attend the Week 6 game between the Steelers and Buccaneers in Tampa. Later in the day, she reported that Trump would not be making the trip .

It would have been the third NFL game attended by Trump during his current term. He was present for Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans between the Chiefs and Eagles. Last year, he attended a Lions-Commanders game in Maryland, making him the first sitting president to attend a regular-season game in nearly 50 years.

Two years ago, in the weeks preceding the election that resulted in his second term, Trump attended a Sunday night game between the Jets and Steelers.

It remains to be seen whether he shows up for an NFL game before the midterm elections, which happen in 20 days. The Commanders are currently scheduled to host the Eagles on Sunday, November 1 — two days before the in-person polls officially open.

articles.title: Bucky Irving amongst most valuable running backs through 5 weeks
articles.summary: Bucky Irving amongst most valuable running backs through 5 weeks
articles.body:
Bucky Irving continues to prove why he is one of the most important players on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Following his dominant performance against the Dallas Cowboys, Irving has established himself as one of the NFL's most impactful running backs, and the advanced analytics back it up. Irving ranks fourth among NFL running backs in rushing Expected Points Added (EPA) through Week 5, sitting at +4.1. Only Kenneth Walker III (+10.9), James Cook (+9.1), and Bijan Robinson (+7.0) rank ahead of him. Irving also finds himself ahead of several established stars, including Christian McCaffrey (+2.7), Jahmyr Gibbs (+1.7), Jonathan Taylor (-0.4), Saquon Barkley (-1.7), and Derrick Henry (-9.3).

EPA measures how much a player's rushing production increases or decreases his team's expected points based on down, distance, and field position. Unlike traditional rushing statistics, it helps show whether a running back is actually improving his offense's chances of scoring rather than simply accumulating yards. Irving's ranking is particularly impressive given Tampa Bay's offensive struggles at the start of the season. The Buccaneers have dealt with inconsistent play calling, difficulty sustaining drives, and a quarterback change following Baker Mayfield's thumb injury. Despite those challenges, Irving has remained one of the few offensive players capable of consistently creating opportunities. His Week 5 performance against Dallas was the perfect example. Irving rushed for a career-high 165 yards on 21 carries, averaging 7.9 yards per attempt while helping Tampa Bay secure its first victory of the season. His ability to turn ordinary rushing attempts into explosive gains completely changed the dynamic of the Buccaneers' offense.

Tampa Bay isn't simply benefiting from giving him the football. His production is helping put the offense in better situations, creating scoring opportunities and taking pressure off rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. For offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, the message should be clear. Irving isn't just another piece of the offense. He is arguably its most important weapon, and his efficiency makes a strong case for continuing to build the rushing attack around him.

articles.title: Packers Could Lose Josh Jacobs for Much Longer Than Expected Due to NFL Rule
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers should perhaps stop expecting Josh Jacobs to return this season and start preparing to play 2026 without him. The post Packers Could Lo...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers don't know when they might get Josh Jacobs back into the lineup, and the NFL rules are murky and unilateral enough that it is not entirely out of the question that the running back misses most, if not all, of the 2026 campaign.

Jacobs faced a couple of misdemeanor charges, one for battery and one for criminal damage to property, following a domestic incident with his former girlfriend in Wisconsin back in May. He pleaded no contest to both charges on September 10, after which the judge handed down punishments that do not include jail time.

The RB's lawyers expedited the hearing in order to wrap the matter up prior to the start of the regular season, which they accomplished. The NFL has typically handed out suspensions in the realm of six games for the type of off-field concerns Jacobs' actions bring with them.

So that was the assumption around the league — that commissioner Roger Goodell would issue a six-to-eight game suspension without pay and Jacobs would return at some point between Weeks 7-9. But with Week 6 just around the corner, the NFL has issued no ruling and Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which is the equivalent of paid leave.

The reason involves video footage of the interaction between Jacobs and his former girlfriend, which the league wants to review before making its determinations. The victim in the case asked the court to seal that evidence permanently, which would have ended the matter. But the judge declined, referring that decision back to the investigating police department that collected the evidence.

There was both an update on that process as well as the revelation of a stipulation in the league's code of conduct policy on Tuesday that indicate Jacobs' absence could stretch on indefinitely.

NFL Still Unable to Review Video Evidence From Josh Jacobs' Legal Case

First, Rob Demovsky of ESPN authored a summary of the police department's decision on the NFL's petition to view the evidence via a public records request.

"An update from the Hobart/Lawrence police department in response to a FOIA request by ESPN for the records in the Josh Jacobs case," Demovsky posted to X Tuesday, October 13 . "To summarize, they determined that 'certain records could be released with appropriate redactions' but that one or more parties (presumably Jacobs and/or the victim) have appealed that decision and therefore nothing will be immediately released."

More or less, that means it could be several more weeks, or even months, before the process is complete and the police release the footage to the NFL — if they ever do. And while this holds off any suspension for Jacobs and allows him to continue on in gainful employment as a member of the Packers organization, it also creates an ongoing obstacle to his return to the field.

NFL May Attempt to Force Josh Jacobs Into Revealing Video Evidence, Even if Legal Process Permanently Seals It

Ken Ingalls, who studies the Green Bay salary cap and reports/posts his work on social media, noted another quirk in the case that fans may sometimes forget, or may not be aware of in the first place.

"Josh Jacobs still sits on the Exempt List, and the video release is still the holdup," Ingalls posted to X on Tuesday . "The league operates on their own standards. Even if the video gets sealed by the legal process, they can still ask/expect Jacobs to willingly share this to them as part of their investigation."

The league can, and has, demanded access to players' and coaches' phone records and other private information in the course of previous investigations involving its code of conduct policy.

It is unclear whether Jacobs still has any copy of the video evidence in question in his possession. If he does, and if the court seals it as evidence not to be shared publicly, which would benefit Jacobs and also appears to be what he wants based on Demovsky's report, it is unclear if the NFL could legally compel the running back to hand over that footage by holding his career hostage.

The unfortunate point for Packers fans is that the sport's worst run game through five weeks ( 60.4 yards per game average and two touchdowns total) does not appear likely to welcome back its RB1 anytime soon.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill found liable for 2 battery counts, jury awards $500,000 to NFL star's estranged wife
articles.summary: A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro.
articles.body: MIAMI — A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro — ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife. Hill, who has played for the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery — one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025. The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages. The jury found Hill, 32, not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence. The trial involved allegations of abuse made by Vaccaro, 30, who on the stand described instances in which Hill allegedly pulled her hair and “treated me like I was, just, a man.” Hill took the stand last week and mostly denied what he called “false allegations” made by his estranged wife, while saying in one instance he shoved Vaccaro and “created a hole in the wall." Hill, wearing a dark polo shirt on Tuesday, embraced one of his attorneys and shook hands with others following the verdict before leaving the courtroom by himself. It wasn't immediately clear what the verdict means for Hill's return to the NFL. He is still working his way back from a dislocated knee and torn ligaments suffered in September 2025 while he was with the Dolphins, but his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that he could be ready to play by November.

articles.title: Bears' Caleb Williams Changes IG Profile Photo to John Wick Amid Injury Rehab, 'I'm Inevitable'
articles.summary: Chicago Bears star quarterback Caleb Williams appears to have vengeance on his mind as he works his way back from his hamstring injury.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears star quarterback Caleb Williams appears to have vengeance on his mind as he works his way back from his hamstring injury.

Williams changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick and updated his bio to "I'm inevitable."

Played by Keanu Reeves, Wick is the title character of one of the greatest action film series in recent memory. The hitman has often sought revenge after being dragged back into the criminal underworld after retiring.

It appears that Williams is ready to channel that energy when he gets back on the field after missing the past three games. The Bears won their first two games without him but are coming off a disappointing 31-7 loss to the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson said earlier this week that the team's starting quarterback for Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons hasn't yet been determined, and the team's quick turnaround against the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football could be a reason to hold out Williams for another week.

Still, it's clear that Williams is motivated to return sooner rather than later, so he will likely try to push himself to make it back in time for the game against the Falcons.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill in Contract Talks With NFL Teams Amid Landing Spot Rumors, Injury Rehab
articles.summary: There are reportedly multiple teams interested in free agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill as he continues to rehab from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign.
articles.body:
There are reportedly multiple teams interested in free agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill as he continues to rehab from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday that Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he is still talking with multiple teams even though "nothing is imminent at this time. He's continuing his rehab with the goal of being on a team in the immediate future."

Earlier this month, Michael Silver of The Athletic reported the Kansas City Chiefs were "very interested" in a reunion with Hill, which would make sense.

After all, there is already chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes after Hill played for the AFC West team from 2016 through 2021. He helped the Chiefs win the Super Bowl during the 2019 campaign and was one of the best receivers in the league during that span.

What's more, Kansas City needs wide receiver depth with Tyquan Thornton (ankle) and Rashee Rice (hamstring) dealing with injuries.

Silver also reported Hill was "targeting a November return" from the significant knee injury he suffered that included a dislocation and torn ACL.

That multiple teams would be interested in a 32-year-old coming off such a serious injury is a testament to his past production. Hill's resume includes five First-Team All-Pro selections, eight Pro Bowl nods, six seasons with more than 1,100 receiving yards and three seasons with double-digit touchdown catches.

He led the league in receiving yards (1,799) and touchdown catches (13) during the 2023 campaign with the Miami Dolphins.

Still, he failed to reach the 1,000-yard mark in 2024 and played just four games in 2025 because of the injury. There are plenty of question marks surrounding him, including whether he will still be the same playmaker if his speed is impacted by his age and recovery.

For now, he remains a free agent. But he is apparently generating plenty of interest from around the league.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Dan Quinn's Commanders Hot Seat After End-of-Game Blunder vs. Giants
articles.summary: Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn is expected to "get some time to turn things around" after a costly offensive miscommunication late in Sunday's overtime tie against the New York Giants, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn is expected to "get some time to turn things around" after a costly offensive miscommunication late in Sunday's overtime tie against the New York Giants, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

Fowler noted how much runway Quinn will get after his team's 1-3-1 start to the 2026 season "is uncertain."

"In the short term, Quinn plans to improve communication with staff and players to ensure this doesn't happen again," Fowler reported. "Quinn and his staff practice game-day situations frequently, and he consults his coaches on situations before each drive and throughout drives.

"But, clearly, something was missed this time, and Quinn plans to improve, among other things, in-week stress points with his coordinators."

Fowler predicted the Commanders' performance in the three games remaining before the trade deadline will impact the franchise's view of Quinn going forward.

The Commanders are playing at the San Francisco 49ers next Monday before a Week 7 bye.

Washington will then return home for Sunday games against the Philadelphia Eagles and Los Angeles Rams before general manager Adam Peters has to commit to a direction ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Quinn is in the third year of his tenure with the Commanders, which began with an NFC title run in Jayden Daniels' 2024 rookie campaign but was derailed in 2025 amid the quarterback's injury issues.

Daniels again struggled with consistency and injuries early in the 2026 campaign before the Commanders hit a low point in Week 5. A tied game against the Giants ended when the Commanders offense ran out the clock instead of attempting a potential game-winning 42-yard field goal.

Quinn after told reporters offensive coordinator and first-year playcaller David Blough had made the final call to Daniels, but that responsibility for the late-game gaffe "starts with me."

The tie against the Giants meant the Commanders had won just three of their last 17 games under Quinn dating back to next season.

Quinn said Monday he had spoken to Commanders owner Josh Harris after the tie as part of his normal postgame process.

"No one is pleased with this outcome and where we're at, but the part that we do have, those hard conversations, we're honest about where we're at and what we need to fix," Quinn said Monday.

Quinn will hope to make his case to stick around with the Commanders by showing off improved communication when his team returns to action next Monday in Santa Clara.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Hires Travis Hunter's Agent, Browns QB Wasn't Represented to Start NFL Career
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders now has formal representation after entering the NFL without an agent.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders now has formal representation after entering the NFL without an agent.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sanders will be represented by Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports. The agency also represents his former college teammate, Travis Hunter.

An agent can only do so much for a player who's coming into the league and likely to be drafted. There's little negotiations to be had when the collective bargaining agreement lays out the contract terms for every pick.

Tyreek Hill's Agent Still Talking to Teams

Sanders may have suffered from not having an agent, though.

In hindsight, it's safe to say the former Colorado star took the wrong approach heading into the draft. Then, he didn't have an advocate who could push back against what his dad, Deion, described as "bull junk."

Now into his second season, the need for a dedicated agent has only grown for Sanders.

The 24-year-old's future in Cleveland looks a little shaky based purely on the fact he has backed up Deshaun Watson through the Browns' first five games in 2026.

ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote Wednesday he believes Watson will "keep the job until he gets hurt, he starts to play poorly or Cleveland tumbles out of contention." The NFL insider went on to add that "it would be stunning if the Browns' 2027 starter is someone on the current roster."

If Cleveland tabs a different QB to lead the offense next season, then it will be time for Sanders to begin exploring his options elsewhere. Gauging the trade market, should it come to that, will be easier with an agent.

It's not too early for Sanders to begin thinking about his next contract, either. His rookie deal runs through 2028. He has a lot of work ahead to build up his value before he's eligible for free agency.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Raiders RB's Status Ahead of Game vs. Bills
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has been off to a disappointing start to the 2026 season, and it sounds like he could need some time to rest.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has been off to a disappointing start to the 2026 season, and it sounds like he could need some time to rest.

ESPN's Dan Graziano explained that Jeanty has been hobbled by injuries throughout this year, so the Raiders will eventually give him a week off to recover.

"Jeanty has been bothered by an ankle injury since the preseason and is now dealing with a foot injury as well," Graizano stated. "He was questionable to play Sunday and only got cleared after a nine-minute pregame workout and discussion with team trainers and coaches. But keep an eye on this situation. The Raiders have internally discussed giving Jeanty a week off to heal at some point."

Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak made it clear on Wednesday that Jeanty would be suiting up this week:

Jeanty was limited to 27 yards on 10 carries in Sunday's 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots, though he added 50 receiving yards on three catches. He hasn't rushed for 60 yards or more since his 102-yard performance in Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins, and he hasn't reached the end zone since his two receiving touchdowns in that same game.

Through the first five weeks of the season, the Raiders rank 28th in the NFL with 82.0 rushing yards per game and have scored just two rushing touchdowns. Despite being slowed by his injuries, Jeanty is reportedly pushing to stay on the field.

"He does not want to take a week off and has pushed to play through the injuries," Graziano stated. "But the Raiders' bye isn't until Week 13, and there may come a week in the near future where they decide the best thing for Jeanty and for the team is to rest him."

If Jeanty is forced to sit out at any point, Graziano noted that the Raiders "have confidence in rookie running back Mike Washington Jr.'s ability to hold things down for a game or two with Dylan Laube backing him up, if it came to that."

The Raiders (3-2) will be hoping to avoid a three-game losing streak, but they will face a tough test in Week 6 against the Buffalo Bills (4-1).

articles.title: “It’s really cool to see kids thinking about other people”: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies’ Volunteer for 15 program encourages meaningful youth community service

articles.body: Kids are our future. If they spend all their time on themselves or on gadgets, they won’t understand the importance of community service or what it feels like to help others.“I think so many kids in middle school and high school don’t realize how much of an impact they can make in their own communities by helping others.I’m inspired by the YVC [Youth Volunteer Corps] youth volunteers, and I can’t wait to see what they accomplish this summer,” Patrick Mahomes said during the Volunteer for 15 launch.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes encourage youth community servicePatrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies teamed up with the Youth Volunteer Corps for the Volunteer for 15 program.The program encourages youth to make a difference in their own communities. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Chargers, Potential Deadline Candidates Amid Justin Herbert Buzz
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers didn't enter the 2026 season as obvious selling candidates ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline, but they could be facing a new reality following an 0-5 start.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers didn't enter the 2026 season as obvious selling candidates ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline, but they could be facing a new reality following an 0-5 start.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that Los Angeles "is drawing the most intrigue from rival teams" amid the three 0-5 clubs since the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans "are clearly mid-rebuild" and were more known commodities coming into the season.

While Fowler pointed out many around the league have "a deep affinity for" quarterback Justin Herbert, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Tuesday that he spoke with someone with the Chargers about the idea of trading the signal-caller and was met with immediate resistance.

Jury Finds Tyreek Hill Liable for 2 Battery Counts (AP)

"The person basically cut me off mid-sentence, stopped me in my tracks, and said, 'let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence should we trade Justin Herbert has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'"

With Herbert seemingly off the board, Fowler highlighted Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu as possible trade candidates even though there aren't "a ton of obvious" ones on the roster.

This is likely something of an adjustment period for the Chargers' front office, as the team is coming off back-to-back playoff appearances and has been in the postseason in three of the last four years.

It likely expected to be competitive and in the playoff mix this season with Herbert, head coach Jim Harbaugh and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, but that has been anything but the case.

That means the front office may need to adjust on the fly and embrace some of the selling conversations it surely wasn't expecting to have not that long ago.

"I think it's going to be really difficult for them to admit when and if they need to trade guys," an executive with another team told Fowler.

That could be good news for teams in need of pass-rush additions with Mack and Tuipulotu, and rival clubs will surely continue watching the Chargers to see how the situation unfolds before the deadline.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Trade to Texans Questioned by Insiders in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Some NFL evaluators feel the Houston Texans potentially overpaid to acquire third-year wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Some NFL evaluators feel the Houston Texans potentially overpaid to acquire third-year wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

Fowler reported "the belief among league evaluators we consulted is that Houston didn't have much true, known competition for Marvin Harrison Jr. because of what Texans GM Nick Caserio was willing to give up to get him."

The Texans traded a 2027 second-round pick, and swapped a 2027 sixth-rounder for a 2027 seventh-round selection, in order to acquire Harrison from the Cardinals.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported prior to the deal the Cardinals had "told inquiring teams that it wanted first-round value in return for Harrison."

Fowler reported some teams saw the inclusion of even a 2027 second-rounder as a "nonstarter" in a potential deal.

"Multiple teams consulted believe that Harrison, despite his billing as the 2024 No. 4 overall pick, was probably worth a fourth-round pick when considering his declining play and his lack of competition on routes at times this season," Fowler reported.

The Indianapolis Colts were one team dissuaded by the Cardinals' price, per Fowler. The Kansas City Chiefs have also looked for wide receivers but "were not considered major players" for Harrison, Fowler added.

Harrison, 24, made five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown while receiving 13 targets over four games as Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett leaned on Trey McBride and Michael Wilson.

Fowler concluded Caserio completing the trade despite that limited usage was part of an "aggressive" approach to build around Harrison's former Ohio State teammate, C.J. Stroud.

Caserio seemingly showed some hesitancy about a long-term commitment to Stroud by allowing him to head into the penultimate season of his rookie contract without an extension.

The Texans have since gotten off to a 1-4 start to the 2026 campaign in part thanks to ranking among the NFL's least effective passing defensives. Stroud has nonetheless completed 64.3 percent of his passes for 1,402 passing yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions.

Stroud will look to help his case for a long-term deal, while Harrison will look to revitalize his career by getting more targets, when this former Buckeyes duo reunites in Sunday's Week 6 matchup at the Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: WWE's The Miz Challenges Tom Brady, Rob Gronkowski to Tag-Team Match With Logan Paul
articles.summary: Former NFL star Rob Gronkowski may have unwittingly signed up legendary quarterback Tom Brady for a wrestling match.
articles.body:
Former NFL star Rob Gronkowski may have unwittingly signed up legendary quarterback Tom Brady for a wrestling match.

During an appearance on the Up & Adams podcast alongside WWE Superstar The Miz, Gronkowski boldly declared his intentions to challenge The Miz in the wrestling ring.

"I'm gonna come back and I'm gonna just beat the crap out of your ugly face in that ring, dude, just smack you all around," Gronkowski said.

However, The Miz took things a step further, telling Gronkowski to bring Brady along for a tag team match against him and Logan Paul.

"You go and get your little Tommy boy. I'll tell you what, I'll get Logan Paul and we'll take you both on in a tag team and we'll wipe the floor with both of you," The Miz retorted. "Bing bang boom, see ya, bye."

For his part, Gronkowski didn't flinch after The Miz upped the ante.

Brady and Paul had a brief feud earlier this year before facing each other in a flag football game. They then had a kayfabe confrontation at Fanatics Fest over the summer that saw Brady slap the former WWE United States Champion.

If Paul and Brady eventually decide to settle their differences in the ring, Gronkowski made it clear that he will be in his former quarterback's corner.

"I don't have beef, it's all Tom. Tom and Logan are the ones that are going at it lately," Gronkowski said. "But if he does start whooping Tom's butt a little bit, I'm gonna have to come in and help him out and be the backup."

articles.title: Chiefs’ interest in Tyreek Hill faces a reality check as verdict complicates reunion hopes before crucial Chargers matchup
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have a clear reason to consider bringing Tyreek Hill back, but a major development off the field has made that decision far more
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs have a clear reason to consider bringing Tyreek Hill back, but a major development off the field has made that decision far more complicated. A Miami jury found Hill liable for two counts of battery against his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, and awarded her $500,000 in compensatory damages. The verdict arrived as Kansas City weighs its options at wide receiver following injuries to key players. With a crucial matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers approaching, the Chiefs need help, but signing Hill could bring uncertainty over his fitness, availability and potential NFL discipline.Tyreek Hill verdict creates new obstacle for Chiefs reunionKansas City's interest in Hill made sense before the verdict. The former Chiefs star knows Andy Reid's offense, has played with Patrick Mahomes and can stretch a defense with his speed. Those qualities are especially valuable now, with injuries disrupting the team's receiving options.Tyquan Thornton suffered a serious ankle injury against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 and was placed on injured reserve. Rashee Rice also picked up a hamstring injury in that game. Hill could offer Mahomes a familiar target and give opposing defenses another player they must account for on every snap.The reunion had also received public support from inside the locker room. Travis Kelce expressed his enthusiasm about the possibility of Hill returning, while defensive tackle Chris Jones also backed the idea. Their comments showed the appeal of reuniting with a player who helped Kansas City win a Super Bowl.But the latest court ruling changes the calculation. The jury found Hill liable for two battery claims tied to incidents in January 2024 and April 2025. It rejected eight other claims and did not award punitive damages. The civil verdict is not a criminal conviction, and its wider impact on Hill's NFL future remains uncertain.For the Chiefs, that uncertainty matters as much as his potential contribution on the field. Signing a player who may face league discipline could leave the team without the help it needs just when the season becomes more demanding.NFL investigation could decide whether Kansas City takes the riskThe NFL's review of Hill under its personal conduct policy remains active. Following the verdict, a league spokesperson said: “We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.”That statement offers no timeline for a decision, leaving Kansas City with an important question: how much of the season could Hill actually play if the team signs him?Hill is also recovering from a serious knee injury suffered in September 2025 while playing for Miami. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that the receiver could be ready to return in November. Even if he reaches full fitness, a possible suspension could reduce the number of games in which he can contribute.That makes the timing awkward. The Chiefs need to address their receiving depth now, not gamble on a player whose availability remains uncertain. They could pursue other options or give younger receivers more responsibility while waiting for clarity from the league.Hill's connection to Kansas City and his history with Mahomes make the reunion appealing. Yet nostalgia cannot settle the practical questions facing general manager Brett Veach and the coaching staff. They must weigh the potential boost against the risk of losing that boost before it has time to matter.The Chargers game adds urgency, but it does not remove those concerns. articles.body: The New England Patriots have a new problem in their backfield after TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain that is expected to keep him out for several weeks. The injury leaves Rhamondre Stevenson carrying more responsibility, with Corey Kiner among the few healthy options behind him. After a 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, New England has reason to feel good about its offense, but losing Henderson limits its depth. That has prompted a trade suggestion involving Arizona Cardinals running back James Conner, a veteran who could help the Patriots stay productive while Henderson recovers.Why the Patriots could trade for James Conner after Henderson’s injuryNBC Boston's Justin Leger has urged New England to consider Conner, whose future in Arizona looks less certain after the Cardinals drafted Jeremiyah Love and signed Tyler Allgeier. Leger pointed to the veteran's uncertain role when he returns from injured reserve, writing:“Conner hasn’t played since Week 3 of last season due to a foot injury. When he returns from IR, which should be soon, he won’t have a clear role on a Cardinals team that drafted rookie phenom Jeremiyah Love and signed the reliable Tyler Allgeier to back him up in the offseason,” wrote Leger.He also stressed that Conner's health should determine whether the Patriots make a move.“Obviously, whether the Patriots should consider acquiring Conner depends entirely on his health status. If he’s ready to make an immediate impact, exploring a trade for him should be a no-brainer.”The argument is easy to understand. Conner offers more than a body to share carries. During the 2024 season, he rushed for 1,094 yards and eight touchdowns, while adding 47 catches for 414 yards and another score. That mix of power running and receiving could give offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels more ways to keep defenses guessing.Conner is also a two-time Pro Bowl selection with experience in Pittsburgh and Arizona. In 110 NFL games, he has averaged 4.4 yards per carry and recorded 72 total touchdowns. Those numbers make him an attractive short-term option, provided he is healthy enough to contribute.Conner could help, but his health makes a trade riskyThe Patriots have reasons to avoid rushing into a deal. Conner is 31 and has not played since suffering a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 of the 2025 season. He managed just 95 rushing yards on 32 carries across three games before going down.That recent history matters. New England would be trading for a player who must first prove he can return to his previous level, not simply relying on his past production. A move only makes sense if the medical outlook supports an immediate role.Henderson's absence still leaves a real gap. As a rookie in 2025, he rushed for 911 yards, averaged 5.1 yards per carry and scored nine rushing touchdowns. His speed gave the Patriots a big-play threat that is difficult to replace with a conventional power back.Stevenson remains capable of handling a larger workload, and his experience gives New England a reliable starting point. But leaning too heavily on him for several weeks could leave the offense short of options if another injury occurs. Kiner may get more chances, though asking an inexperienced player to fill Henderson's role is a different challenge.A late-round draft pick could be a reasonable price for Conner, especially if Arizona is willing to move on from a veteran who has a limited future with the team. Still, the Patriots should not confuse urgency with certainty. Conner could strengthen their backfield, but only if he is ready to play.For a team trying to build on its strong start, the right move is not necessarily the biggest one. New England needs enough depth to protect its offense over the coming weeks, and Conner is worth exploring.
