articles.body:
Lamar Jackson and Ja'Kobi Lane might not be the only star players the Baltimore Ravens are potentially getting back before a Week 6 game against the Cleveland.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday the Ravens are "hopeful" defensive end Trey Hendrickson will make his return from a finger injury this weekend.

Hendrickson's status could change "depending how practice goes," Fowler noted.

Henry, Huntley Win the Game for Ravens 🐦‍⬛

Hendrickson broke a finger on his right hand in the Ravens' season opener. He played two games with the finger taped before undergoing surgery ahead of Week 4.

He and Lane, who has been sidelined since Week 1 with a wrist injury, were both active in the Ravens' Wednesday practice.

Jackson, who is dealing with a left ankle sprain, did not participate in open practice after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported he has a "realistic" chance of returning Sunday.

Hendrickson recorded one sack and a tackle for loss in three games prior to undergoing surgery.

He also added 14 pressures, 10 hurries and three quarterback hits during the Ravens' 2-1 start to the season.

The Ravens did not place Hendrickson on injured reserve after the procedure, indicating the team expected the star edge rusher to miss fewer than four games.

Hendrickson seemed to be wearing a wrap on his right hand in his Wednesday return to practice.

Lane, who made one catch for 11 yards before he was injured in the first half of his NFL debut, did not appear to be wearing his own wrap or brace. His return to practice opened a 21-day window during which the Ravens can move him back to the active roster.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter said in his Monday press conference he felt both Lane and Hendrickson had "put themselves in a real position" to come back for Week 6.

"Trey will be chomping at the bit to be ready to roll this week...We'll see how that shakes out on Wednesday, but I feel pretty good about both those guys," Minter said.

Whether Hendrickson is able to return will determine how much the Ravens lean on outside linebacker Mike Green, who has recorded eight quarterback pressures in his last two games.

Green wasn't the only backup to step up last weekend, when Tyler Huntley helped the Ravens secure an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons while Jackson was sidelined.

If Lane is healthy this Sunday, Minter could look to start working the rookie wideout into the Ravens' offensive game plan regardless of whether Huntley or Jackson gets the nod this Sunday in Cleveland.

articles.title: The fight between the SEC and LSU isn’t over and the Tigers still could be kicked out of the conference
articles.summary: In legalese, the SEC on Tuesday filed a response to LSU’s motion to dismiss a federal lawsuit filed by the conference in September saying that it’s not ready to close the door on the argument because “the dispute remains live.”
articles.body: In legalese, the SEC on Tuesday filed a response to LSU’s motion to dismiss a federal lawsuit filed by the conference in September saying that it’s not ready to close the door on the argument because “the dispute remains live.” In more understandable parenting parlance, the SEC is at the “or else” stage with its troublesome child. Sitting in the driver’s’ seat as LSU misbehaves in the backseat, the SEC is basically saying it will turn this thing around if LSU doesn’t knock it off and behave. At issue: Two months after Lane Kiffin eventually backed down on playing two would-be NFL players after the conference threatened penalties up to – and including – expulsion, men’s basketball coach Will Wade tried and continues to try to add multiple players who have been drafted or gone through the NBA draft in direct conflict to the conference’s policy. “Defendants’ argument that they mooted this case by deciding, at last, not to roster the players is like saying that someone caught with his hand in the cookie jar has cured the problem by pulling it out,” the conference writes in its response. “What’s more, Defendants still have their hands in the jar. LSU’s men’s basketball program continues to defy the Professionalism Rules and its head coach promises to be ‘unapologetic about it.’” At SEC basketball media day the morning after the filing, commissioner Greg Sankey refused to elaborate on the case, saying only, “We will let the filing speak for itself on these issues.” But the commissioner’s tone spoke volumes. He’s not happy, nor is he amused by the school’s insistence to continually thumb its nose at the rules. LSU might view themselves as renegades; the SEC sees them more as outlaws. “I’d like to not be in court,” he said. Speaking to CNN Sports later, Sankey said that the whole sordid thing is “incredibly uncomfortable.” But the commissioner and the league clearly fear they have both no recourse and a real need to protect themselves should LSU continue to try and circumvent its rules. That’s largely based on what Wade has termed his “unconventional” roster-building approach. The coach has recruited three basketball players – R.J. Luis, Saliou Niang and Brice Dessert – who have had varying degrees of NBA involvement. That’s in direct conflict to the SEC’s policy, which states that any athlete who has “previously declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA and did not properly withdraw” cannot compete. Luis, who is actually named in the legal response. signed multiple NBA contracts but won a court injunction in April to play at LSU. A jubilant Wade went to court and celebrated the injunction. On Tuesday, the coach appeared to have gotten his dose of medicine, saying that Luis was “not rostered,” and that the school would follow SEC protocols regarding his eligibility. But when asked during a Zoom specifically about other players, including Niang and Dessert, Wade said he “feel good about that group getting eligible – the ones that were actually on our roster, the ones that were actually on our team, we feel like those guys will get eligible.” Niang, a Senegalese player raised in Italy, was drafted 58th overall in the 2025 NBA draft. Though he did not sign an NBA contract, he appeared in three Summer League games. Dessert, a Frenchman who played professionally overseas, went through the draft process as well in 2025 but went undrafted. Asked specifically about those players, Sankey again reiterated his stance to “let the filing speak for itself.” From the filing: “LSU has also recruited international professional basketball players whose eligibility remains in question. LSU’s head men’s basketball coach has been candid about LSU’s strategy: ‘We’re going to be unapologetic about it. This is who we are. This is what we’re doing. This is the path that we charted. We’re going to go down it, and that’s fine.’” The league has at least put a pause on its initial ask – a temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction to prevent LSU from interfering with the league’s right to vote on the school’s expulsion. But it wants to keep the door open to seek such relief “if and when necessary.” “A live controversy exists between the parties,” the document reads in conclusion. The odds of the league actually expelling LSU are slim. The school is, to put it bluntly, a cash cow. Despite the school’s own reported $26 million deficit, it is a money maker for the SEC, bringing name recognition, tradition, history and a boatload of fans to the table on the regular. The league, however, does have a few arrows in its quiver. In August, when Kiffin was dithering about adding his would-be NFLers, the presidents unanimously (LSU abstained from the vote) approved a new discipline policy for schools that roster NFL, NBA or WNBA players. The penalty options, as reported by ESPN, include a half-season suspension for a coach; a fine up to 50% of the sport’s annual budget and revocation of league voting rights.

articles.title: Mark Sanchez reportedly reaches agreement with truck driver in civil case stemming from stabbing incident in Indianapolis
articles.summary: Last month in the criminal case, Sanchez's legal representatives filed a motion to plead guilty.
articles.body:
Last month, the legal representatives of former NFL quarterback and Fox Sports analyst Mark Sanchez filed a motion to plead guilty in the criminal case that followed an October 2025 incident, in which prosecutors alleged Sanchez was the aggressor prior to him being stabbed.

In recent days, reports have surfaced regarding the matter's corresponding civil case, detailing that the 39-year-old Sanchez, along with Fox Corp., has reached an agreement in principle — it reportedly has yet to be signed — with the truck driver involved in the altercation, which occurred in downtown Indianapolis during the weekend of a Colts game Sanchez was supposed to cover.

The lawyers for the truck driver, Perry Tole — who was 69 at the time of the incident — will file to dismiss the civil case by Jan. 8, according to The Athletic , which cited court filings in its report this week.

That said, the specifics of the agreement have yet to be reported.

Early on Oct. 4, 2025, the day before the Colts clobbered the Las Vegas Raiders in a Week 5 matchup Sanchez was scheduled to call for Fox, Sanchez allegedly confronted Tole, telling him that he was prohibited from parking his truck in an alley between two hotels. Prosecutors said Sanchez tried to enter the truck and knocked down Tole, who claimed to use pepper spray and a knife in self-defense.

Security footage that TMZ obtained last year, days after the news broke, showed Sanchez aimlessly walking, and occasionally stumbling, around the city just past midnight. Sanchez can also be seen running down the alley where Tole was previously spotted parking his truck. In the aftermath of the incident, Tole reportedly said he was doing his job exchanging used cooking oil from the Westin hotel. Tole told police Sanchez smelled of alcohol and had slurred speech.

Also in the aftermath of the altercation, Tole's attorney said his client is " gonna have scars forever " from injuries that included a large gash in Tole's cheek.

Court documents in the civil case note that Tole is seeking damages for suffering "significant injuries to his head, jaw, and neck," per The Athletic.

Sanchez, who wound up recovering from his stab wounds in a nearby hospital, was arrested and reportedly charged with one felony count of battery resulting in serious bodily injury, in addition to misdemeanor charges of unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, public intoxication endangering the life of another and battery resulting in bodily injury.

But the motion Sanchez's representation filed for on Sept. 3 didn't indicate which criminal charges Sanchez will be pleading guilty to, as reported by The Indiana Lawyer , which outlined that a change of plea hearing in the criminal case is slated for Nov. 9 in Marion Superior Court.

Statements provided by attorneys from either side of the civil case last month indicated that a resolution was nearing.

Mott Golitko, a lawyer representing Tole, said in September, according to The Athletic , "Our discussions have been productive, and we're on a positive path toward an agreement that will allow the parties to move forward."

Sanchez spent 10 seasons in the NFL. The New York Jets drafted him No. 5 overall out of USC in 2009. Playing for Rex Ryan, Sanchez quarterbacked the Jets to back-to-back AFC championship games in his first two years in the league.

After five years in New York, Sanchez finished his playing career as a backup, making stops in Philadelphia (2014-15), Dallas (2016), Chicago (2017) and Washington (2018).

articles.title: Washington football's all-time passing leader signs with new NFL team
articles.summary: Jake Browning, the Washington Huskies' all-time leading passer, signed with the Los Angeles Chargers on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Washington's career passing leader has landed a new NFL opportunity.

Jake Browning lost the backup quarterback job with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels this preseason and reportedly declined an opportunity to return to the Buccaneers' practice squad to pursue other chances at continuing his NFL career (Browning would currently be the Buccaneers' backup behind Daniels, who has started the last two games for Tampa Bay with Baker Mayfield out with a thumb injury). On Tuesday, that chance came knocking, as Browning reportedly signed with the Los Angeles Chargers after a successful tryout.

Browning will likely be signed to the practice squad as an emergency option behind Chargers quarterbacks Justin Herbert and DJ Uiagalelei. Los Angeles' usual backup, former first-round pick Trey Lance, landed on injured reserve on Saturday with a groin injury, which pulled Uiagalelei up from the practice squad. Browning appears to have beaten out another former Buccaneers quarterback, former second-round selection Kyle Trask, in the tryout, as both were listed as working out for the Chargers alongside five wide receivers.

The Chargers have gotten off to a frustrating start, sitting at 0-5 despite offseason excitement surrounding the hire of former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator to pair with Herbert. The marriage has been a disaster thus far, as Herbert has thrown more interceptions than touchdowns and Los Angeles ranks dead last in offensive EPA/play through five games.

Herbert has also begun to take some hard hits with a number of offensive linemen missing. Left tackle Rashawn Slater, left guard Trey Pipkins III, and center Tyler Biadasz are all on injured reserve, and right tackle Joe Alt left LA's Week 4 game with a neck injury and did not play last week. Herbert took one big shot to the ribs and another to the knee against the Seattle Seahawks in that Week 4 game and took an awkward shot that left him limping this week against the Denver Broncos.

Uiagalelei, whose cousin Ta'ita'i started all 13 games for the Huskies last season and is on Washington's roster this year despite having a preliminary injunction for a fifth season of eligibility overturned, has never seen NFL action after being signed by the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025. Browning, on the other hand, has started 10 games across three seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals with a record of 4-6 while throwing for 2,707 yards, 18 touchdowns, and 15 interceptions.

An interesting oddity will be what jersey number is allocated to Browning. The only available jersey numbers between 0 and 19 are currently 14, 17, 18, and 19. 14 is retired for quarterback Dan Fouts, 18 is retired for wide receiver Charlie Joiner, 19 is retired for wide receiver Lance Alworth, and 17 has not been allocated to a Chargers player since quarterback Philip Rivers retired. The likeliest outcome may be that Browning shares Lance's No. 5 while he is on injured reserve.

articles.title: One NFL Voice Links Damar Hamlin’s Collapse to Stalled 18-Game Season Push
articles.summary: The NFL is in full flow, with 5 weeks of games completed. The league is always looking to improve itself, such as the increased use of international games fo...
articles.body:
The NFL is in full flow, with 5 weeks of games completed. The league is always looking to improve itself, such as the increased use of international games for regular season games to boost the game's popularity.

The league is also trying to expand the regular season games from 17 currently to 18 games a season. However, it has faced obstacles in implementation. One analyst has claimed there is a reason for that.

Damar Hamlin's cardiac arrest could cool NFL's 18-game push

Longtime ESPN commentator Chris Berman stated on October 13, 2026, at Front Office Sports' Tuned In summit that Buffalo Bills safety Damar Hamlin's on-field cardiac arrest back in January 2023 slowed a potential NFL push for an 18-game regular season. Hamlin collapsed after tackling Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins during a Monday Night Football game on January 2, 2023. The incident prompted widespread discussion of player safety and led to the postponement and eventual cancellation of the game.

He said, "The push that might have happened while these current deals were in place—once Damar Hamlin happened, not the time to put it forward. That's my belief. I'm sure I'm not too far off."

The current NFL-NFLPA collective bargaining agreement, ratified in 2020 and extending through the 2030 season (expiring in March 2031), permitted the expansion from 16 to 17 regular-season games in 2021 but does not allow a further increase to 18. An 18-game schedule has been discussed by owners as far back as the 2011 CBA negotiations.

Berman noted the topic is resurfacing as the CBA and media rights deals approach their final years, the NFL can opt out of its television contracts as early as 2030. He observed that the league had remained quiet on the matter for several years due to the need for player approval and the poor optics following the Hamlin episode.

He added, "When the NFL floats stuff, it's not a done deal by any means, but it's a bigger magnitude than what I'm going to say. The NFL is smarter than everybody else. You didn't hear anything about it for a couple years because you'd have to get the players and everyone [to approve], and then maybe with three years left in this TV deal, 'Yeah, we're having 18 games.'" According to Front Office Sports, both the NFL and ESPN declined comment on Berman's remarks.

It remains to be seen whether the NFL will advocate for an 18-game season.

articles.title: Chargers Sign QB With 2,700 Career Yards as Pressure Mounts on Justin Herbert
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are adding a veteran quarterback to their practice squad after an injury left the team short on depth at the position. The signing g...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are adding a veteran quarterback to their practice squad after an injury left the team short on depth at the position.

The signing gives the team another option at quarterback, though he must be added to the active roster before he can play.

Chargers add veteran quarterback to backup group

The Los Angeles Chargers have struggled to start the 2026 season, holding an 0–5 record after losing their first five games. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that the team is signing quarterback Jake Browning to its practice squad.

"The Chargers are signing veteran QB Jake Browning, per source," Pelissero reported .

Browning entered the NFL in 2019 as an undrafted free agent with the Minnesota Vikings after playing college football at the University of Washington. He spent time on Minnesota's practice squad before joining the Cincinnati Bengals in 2021, where he remained through 2022 and earned a place on the 53-player roster in 2023.

Browning received his first extended starting opportunity that season after Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow suffered a season-ending injury. He started seven games, throwing for 1,868 yards and 11 touchdowns while completing 71.5% of his passes. Across the full season, he finished with 1,936 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions, along with 127 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns.

His role changed in 2024, when he appeared in three games without attempting a pass. The following season, he played five games and started three for Cincinnati, completing 81 of 125 passes for 771 yards and six touchdowns while throwing eight interceptions.

Browning signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on March 13, 2026, but did not make their final roster after the preseason. He has appeared in 17 regular-season NFL games, including 10 starts, and recorded 2,707 passing yards, 18 touchdowns, 15 interceptions and a 68.5% completion rate.

Browning joins a quarterback room led by Justin Herbert . Before the signing, rookie D.J. Uiagalelei was the only other healthy quarterback on the active roster. Browning's time as a starter in Cincinnati adds another quarterback with NFL starts to the roster, although his practice squad status does not automatically make him eligible to play.

Trey Lance's placement on injured reserve left the Chargers with one healthy backup quarterback on the active roster. Browning must be added to the active roster before he can appear in a game.

Chargers' injury list includes several key starters

The Los Angeles Chargers have several players on injured reserve, including left tackle Rashawn Slater , offensive linemen Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins, center Tyler Biadasz, and quarterback Trey Lance. Lance has a groin injury, Slater has an ankle injury, and Penning was placed on injured reserve after suffering a concussion.

Wide receiver Quentin Johnston was ruled out against Denver with a chest injury. He had seven catches for 108 yards through the first four games of the season. Safety Derwin James also missed that game with a hamstring injury after recording 21 tackles, including 12 solo tackles, in his first three games. Cornerback Donte Jackson was ruled out with a hamstring injury.

Offensive tackle Joe Alt missed the Denver game with a neck injury after starting the first three games of the season. Guard Kayode Awosika was also out with a fibula injury. These players' injuries have kept them out of action for varying periods.

The Chargers added quarterback Jake Browning to their practice squad after Trey Lance was placed on injured reserve. The Chargers will face the Kansas City Chiefs on October 18 at Arrowhead Stadium.

The Chicago Bears are hitting the silver screen this fall. They will be the subject of a new Hallmark Christmas movie , Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story.

On Tuesday, Caleb Williams , Colston Loveland , and others attended an exclusive premiere at the Gorton Center in Lake Forest, Illinois.

However, head coach Ben Johnson was a no-show , per Adam Hoge of CHGO Bears. When asked if he was attending the premiere, Johnson said: "Not a chance."

It turns out Johnson isn't too thrilled about the movie, both when announcing it back in the summer and when taking a break from watching film. However, Johnson does make a cameo appearance.

The film follows freelance reporter Avery, played by Lyndsy Fonseca, who gets an assignment to profile Darlene, played by Marsha Mason, as she gears up to attend her 500th Bears game. Along the way, Avery develops a romance with Darlene's grandson Matt, played by Robert Buckley, a Chicago firefighter.

Loveland and Cole Kmet make cameos, as do Bears legends Mike Singletary, Charles Tillman, and Dan Hampton.

The Bears are among the most visible NFL teams to make strong inroads into popular culture. It all began with the "Super Bowl Shuffle" in 1985 with Walter Payton, Jim McMahmmon, Richard Dent, and William Perry. The Bears insignia appeared in sitcoms such as Roseanne and was a central theme in the iconic Saturday Night Live skit "Superfans," which paid homage to the late coach Mike Ditka .

Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story debuts on the Hallmark Channel on October 17 .

articles.title: Cowboys Reverse Recent Cuts With Triple Roster Adjustments Ahead of Packers Rivalry
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys made roster changes Tuesday ahead of their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers. The moves include two players returning after recent...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys made roster changes Tuesday ahead of their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers . The moves include two players returning after recent roster decisions.

The Cowboys also released cornerback Alex Austin from their practice squad as they prepare for the upcoming matchup.

Cowboys make changes across their roster

The Dallas Cowboys made three roster moves Tuesday, October 13, ahead of their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers. The Cowboys re-signed running back Emari Demercado to the 53-man roster, signed guard Nick Leverett to the practice squad and released cornerback Alex Austin from the practice squad. The Cowboys are 2–3 after a 24–16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Cowboys announced the moves in a statement : "The @dallascowboys signed RB Emari Demercado on Tuesday. The club also signed G Nick Leverett to the practice squad and released CB Alex Austin from the practice squad."

Demercado was waived October 8 to make room for guard Tyler Smith, who returned from injured reserve before the Buccaneers game. The Cowboys brought him back five days later.

Demercado joined the Arizona Cardinals as an undrafted free agent in 2023 after playing at TCU. He signed a three-year, $2.71 million contract with the Cardinals, including a $915,000 base salary in 2024. Following the 2025 season, he signed a one-year deal with the Kansas City Chiefs during the 2026 offseason but was released during final roster cuts. The Cowboys claimed him off waivers August 31. His current contract terms with the Cowboys have not been publicly disclosed.

He has played in two games for the Cowboys this season, recording five carries for 15 rushing yards. In 2025, he played 13 games for the Cardinals with 44 carries for 312 rushing yards, 13 catches for 101 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown. He had 223 rushing yards in 2024 and 284 in 2023. During three Cowboys preseason games, he recorded 17 carries for 64 rushing yards and two catches for 23 receiving yards. Malik Davis suffered a season-ending hip injury before Week 1, creating another opportunity in the Cowboys' running back group.

Leverett was waived October 12 and re-signed to the practice squad Tuesday. The Cowboys had promoted him to the active roster September 9 after Tyler Smith went on injured reserve. He played in all five games this season, mainly on special teams.

The 28-year-old has five years of NFL experience after playing at Rice. He can play center and guard and previously played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals. He has appeared in 24 NFL games during his career.

Austin signed with the Miami Dolphins March 12, 2026, and was released August 29. The Cowboys added him to their practice squad September 30 before releasing him October 13. The Buffalo Bills drafted him 252nd overall in the seventh round in 2023. He also played for the Houston Texans and New England Patriots. In three seasons with those two teams, he played 29 games with six starts. His career totals are 27 tackles, one interception and eight passes defended. He spent the offseason with Miami before later joining Dallas' practice squad.

The Cowboys have also adjusted their roster this season, including trading for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and activating Tyler Smith from injured reserve. The team has also moved players between the active roster and practice squad. Schottenheimer has faced criticism over some of the team's decisions this season.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously said , "There'll be some roster adjustments you guys will see. Some will be more noticeable than others, and some will be subtle as you look at it."

The Cowboys will face the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 18. The two teams have a long NFL rivalry and have met several times in the playoffs. The Cowboys are 2–3, while the Packers are 3–2.

articles.title: Rams Receive Fresh Update on Myles Garrett’s Knee Injury Status
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are sitting at 2-3 after a Monday night overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the defense is still waiting on its biggest offseason ad...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are sitting at 2-3 after a Monday night overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the defense is still waiting on its biggest offseason addition, pass rusher Myles Garrett . He has watched from the sideline since opening week. With Arizona next on the schedule, the latest word from NFL Network about his recovery offers a clearer look at when he may finally return.

Myles Garrett return timeline points to Week 7

NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport said Tuesday on The Rich Eisen Show that Myles Garrett is closing in on a return. Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery the Monday after the Rams' Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and was placed on injured reserve with an estimated recovery of about six weeks.

Rapoport noted that Garrett was visible on the Rams' sideline during Monday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills while still recovering.

"Week 7 should be around when he's ready, which could mean practicing this week and then playing next week. Or it could mean somehow practicing this week—we're getting to the window," Rapoport told Eisen. That timeline points to the Rams' game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25.

Although Garrett is already eligible to come off injured reserve, but he is not yet ready to practice. Head coach Sean McVay said Tuesday that the Rams will not open Garrett's 21-day practice window this week, meaning he will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.

The latest comments provide a clearer target for Garrett's return , even as the team remains deliberately cautious.

McVay had said Saturday that the surgery went well and Garrett is making good progress, emphasizing that the goal is a full return to performance rather than simply a return to the field.

In the meantime, Josiah Stewart has assumed a larger share of the pass-rush snaps. However, Garrett's eventual return would deliver a significant boost to the Rams' defense, especially given the substantial investment Los Angeles made to acquire him.

In a major offseason trade, the Rams acquired Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for established pass rusher Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a 2027 first-round selection.

The 30-year-old arrived as the reigning Defensive Player of the Year after posting a record 23 sacks the previous season. His limited impact in the season-opening game in Australia highlighted why the Rams are determined to ensure he is fully healthy before returning to the field.

Myles Garrett's tough Rams debut in Australia

Garrett played through knee swelling in the opener, a 27-7 loss in Melbourne, after missing most of training camp. He had five quarterback pressures but no sacks and no tackles. According to ESPN Research, it was only the fourth tackle-less game of his career.

Garrett called it "the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

"I've got to be better. I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before," Garrett said . Surgery followed within days, and the Rams have gone 2-2 without him.

Before the season, Los Angeles was widely seen as a Super Bowl favorite, and Garrett was a major reason why. The Rams beat the Eagles in Week 4 to stay afloat, but penalties and special teams problems hurt them against Buffalo. His return would give them a pass rush they have yet to see at full strength.

The Rams (2-3) host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 18, still without Garrett. Los Angeles needs a win to steady its season, while Arizona looks for a divisional upset. Next comes the Raiders, a game that could finally bring Garrett back.

articles.title: Carnell Tate Drops Honest Quote as Cam Ward, Titans Struggle Amid Winless 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate provided honest commentary to reporters about how he feels amid the team's difficult 0-5 start and what he's doing to handle it.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate provided honest commentary to reporters about how he feels amid the team's difficult 0-5 start and what he's doing to handle it.

ESPN's Turron Davenport asked Tate, who experienced great success and winning at Ohio State (including a national championship), what it's like to deal with the losing.

"It's rough," Tate said. "I ain't never lose like this in my life, so we just trying to turn it around for real, for real."

When Davenport asked what he's doing to deal with it, Tate said: "I'm just staying focused on what I can controlling what I can control. As long as you can do your 1/11th, each person do their 1/11th, we can go out there and win some games."

Tennessee is one of three teams to start 0-5 this year alongside the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers. The Titans have scored the league's fewest points per game (11.6), and the offense is very much a work-in-progress. Per Ian Hartitz of Rotowire, the Titans are the only team that hasn't completed a pass of 30 or more yards downfield.

Tennessee's low point occurred on Sunday, when the Titans lost 26-3 to the previously winless Houston Texans. Houston out-gained Tennessee 329-187.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward spoke with reporters about a meeting he had with head coach Robert Saleh this week.

The Titans hope for their first victory on Sunday when they visit the Indianapolis Colts.

articles.body:
It hasn't taken wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. very long to rediscover his chemistry with star quarterback C.J. Stroud.

After being traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans earlier this week, Harrison was on the field catching passes from Stroud during Wednesday's practice:

Stroud and Harrison starred together at Ohio State before reaching the NFL, with Harrison producing career bests of 77 catches, 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns during their final season together in 2022.

The Texans are hoping that Stroud and Harrison will be able to recreate their magic together as the team tries to bounce back from a 1-4 start to the 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Everything Marvin Harrison Jr. Said About Texans-Cardinals Trade, Stroud, Viral Route-Running Videos
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. is excited for a fresh start in Houston.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. is excited for a fresh start in Houston.

The veteran wide receiver spoke to reporters for the first time since he was traded to the Texans alongside a 2027 sixth-round pick for a 2026 second- and seventh-rounder, saying he was looking forward to his new situation:

"Great situation for me, being with quarterback you have rapport with," he told reporters referencing C.J. Stroud, his teammate at Ohio State.

As for what went wrong with the Arizona Cardinals, Harrison kept things close to the vest.

"I'll keep those things to myself," he told reporters . "I'm really just moving forward."

He also said he was able to lean on his father, Hall of Fame wideout Marvin Harrison, during the ordeal.

"We had that understanding, football is always a business," he told reporters .

Harrison, 24, was an incredibly hyped prospect coming out of Ohio State and was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. His rookie season was promising (62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns), but injuries cost him five games in 2025, his production was down and this season he seemed to be an afterthought in Arizona's offense.

Whether it was simply a poor fit or Harrison was dramatically overrated coming out of college remains to be seen. His quarterback clearly believes it was the former.

"It doesn't matter what people say," Stroud told reporters . "He's a heckuva player. I don't agree with some of the things people are saying about him. They can have their opinions. It doesn't really affect you unless you let it. He'll be fine. He's a confident dude. He'll be fine."

articles.title: Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. Discusses Throwing Up Before Missing Bucs Game, 'It Was Brutal'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. described the illness that forced him to miss the team's 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. described the illness that forced him to miss the team's 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5.

"I was throwing up outside my Uber on the way to the game," Porter said Wednesday, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "It was brutal."

The 26-year-old has appeared in one game for the Cowboys since they acquired him in an Oct. 1 trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Porter is expecting to make his return during Dallas' upcoming matchup with the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, per Machota.

He was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday.

Porter didn't suit up for the Steelers to start the 2026 season, as he was attempting to land a new contract from Pittsburgh while also dealing with back issues .

In his first appearance with the Cowboys, he played 25 snaps during their 34-30 win over the Houston Texans in Week 4.

Following Dallas' eventual defeat at the hands of Tampa Bay with Porter unavailable, head coach Brian Schottenheimer discussed the cornerback's absence.

"Unique thing, came to the stadium and he wasn't feeling very well," Schottenheimer said, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "The trainers came to us, said it got significantly worse after they treated him. He just wasn't feeling good. And the decision was made that he wasn't going to be able to play as he was very, very sick."

The Cowboys are hoping that Porter can provide a boost to their struggling secondary, as they've allowed opposing quarterbacks to post a 109.6 passer rating against them (via Pro Football Reference ).

Porter served as a key piece of Pittsburgh's defense in 2025, recording 52 tackles across 14 games. He also ranked No. 12 among all players with 14 passes defended.

Porter and the Cowboys are set to face the Packers on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tomi Lahren suggests Tony Romo to listen to the advice he gave her during 2016 Trevor Noah backlash
articles.summary: Tomi Lahren revealed Tony Romo once gave her advice about handling online hate, words the former Dallas Cowboys signal caller now needs himself.
articles.body: Former NFL quarterback Tony Romo's life has been a bit of a roller coaster these days. The four-time Pro Bowl selection recently parted ways with CBS, citing the need to take a mental health break. This came just a few short months after he was arrested on charges of OWI in Wisconsin back in July, and happened the same day he was booted from the Korn Ferry qualifier for signing an incorrect scorecard. It's probably safe to say that 2026 has not been Romo's year, but if anyone knows how to handle rough times amid public scrutiny, it's the former Dallas Cowboys signal-caller. JIM NANTZ SPEAKS OUT ON 'GREAT FRIEND' TONY ROMO'S OWI ARREST, SAYS HE WILL 'ALWAYS' BE THERE FOR HIM And OutKick's very own Tomi Lahren has proof. During an episode of "Tomi Lahren is Fearless," Lahren explained to her guest, Barstool's Kevin "KFC" Clancy, that Romo once offered up some sage advice about dealing with online hate. "It was actually Tony Romo at the time who told me, 'you think the whole world is talking about it, but really, nobody is,'" Lahren recounts. This came on the heels of Lahren receiving some hateful comments for her appearance on "The Daily Show with Trevor Noah" just after Donald Trump won in 2016. "Basically the message was, 'don't be so full of yourself that you think that everybody is talking about you,'" Lahren relayed. "Because most people aren't even on the internet." Clancy concurred and took things even one step further. "I think humans are not meant to be this connected and interact this much," he opined. "We can't handle it." The longtime Barstool employee goes on to explain that for 99.9% of human history, we as humans were only confined to interacting with our small community. COWBOYS OWNER JERRY JONES HAS TONY ROMO'S BACK, BELIEVES HE WILL 'WORK THROUGH' OWI ARREST "The fact that you have access to millions of people's opinions ... I don't think we are even wired to be able to handle that." It's great advice from all parties involved, and Romo would be wise to heed the words he offered up to Lahren nearly a decade ago. He's going through a rough patch, but he will come out on the other side. A guy as resilient as Romo is — undrafted from a small school in Eastern Illinois, coming back from a number of injuries — will be able to rebound just fine. No one knows what the future holds for the former CBS commentator, but as for the noise online in the present, 46-year-old Romo just needs to listen to the 36-year-old version of himself. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "You think the whole world is talking about it, but really, nobody is."

articles.title: Ravens vs Falcons: the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
articles.summary: The Ravens are officially on a win streak after stealing one from Atlanta.
articles.body:
In a thrilling overtime win, the Baltimore Ravens managed to top the Atlanta Falcons despite missing Lamar Jackson. The 30-23 win moved the Ravens to 4-1 in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. It was mostly good on Sunday night, with two glaring issues:

Backup quarterback situation: Fans were caught up in the Joe Fagnano hype during the preseason, but in Atlanta, Tyler Huntley reminded the NFL world why he is Lamar Jackson's backup. He wasn't perfect and waited to fully turn it on until the end of the game, but Huntley simply knows how to win as a spot starter. He's now 3-0 in his starts dating back to last season. When the Ravens needed a quick drive and couldn't lean on the run, Huntley drove the Ravens 71 yards in under two minutes to tie the game. When they needed to kill clock, he confidently commanded the offense down the field. The dude is simply a gamer who does what is needed to win.

The WR trio: Zay Flowers with eight catches and 53 yards. Rashod Bateman with five catches and 62 yards. Tez Walker with the back shoulder fade ball touchdown catch. The Ravens needed offensive skill players to step up with Lamar Jackson out and the wide receivers did just that. This passing game officially runs through them, and now they're finally getting Ja'Kobi Lane in the mix, too.

Run defense: Michael Penix came into Sunday's game hot, but the entire football world that the Ravens would have to find a way to stop (or at least slow) the even-hotter Bijan Robinson to beat the Falcons. Robinson is the best running back in the NFL this season and a monster primetime performer. He had games of 194 and 145 yards coming into this one since Penix's return. And instead of allowing him to tote the rock all night, gashing them for first down after first down, and draining the clock, the Ravens held him to 86 yards. They allowed rushes of 20 and 38 yards and otherwise kept a lid on his carries. Baltimore also contained Robinson in the red zone and didn't allow him to score.

The coaching staff: This was a big moment for this new young staff. No Lamar Jackson, no Trey Hendrickson, a reshuffled offensive line, on the road, in primetime, against a red-hot team. All of those questinos, and the coaching staff answered. Jesse Minter and Anthony's Weaver's defense kept this game in striking distance all night, only allowing one defensive touchdown and containing Robinson. Declan Doyle dialed up plays and kept the game simple for Huntley. This staff made a plan that gave this team a chance to win.

Third-and-long defense: The most concerning negative out of this game was the third-down defense. It continues to be a problem. The Ravens allowed multiple third-and-10s, a third-and-11, and a third-and-15 to be converted. The plan was clearly to force Penix to beat them after shutting down Robinson in the run game, and Penix did, multiple times, often to Drake London, the Falcons' No. 1 receiver. Coverage on the back end still seems to be struggling if the rush doesn't get home on third down. Jesse Minter took the blame on himself, saying his play calling left them in bad spots.

Either way, it's an issue that has to get fixed, and I believe it will. Trey Hendrickson returning to the lineup will help out a ton. It's also something that will simply get better with time as Minter and the defense get more comfortable in their identity. As the comparison that everyone wants to look to, Mike Macdonald's defense in Seattle struggled their first season as Macdonald adjusted to being a headcoach and a play calling while installing his vision. Minter's unit will adapt.

Mark Andrews: I have been an advocate for Mark Andrews' play this season. Not to say that I agreed with the decision to re-sign him, but Mark Andrews is still very much capable of playing the tight end position. He is still a good blocker and capable of being a possession tight end, as we saw in the last couple of weeks. But what occurred on Sunday was atrocious and near malpractice. Mark Andrews directly influenced a 13-point swing in favor of Atlanta. First, a dropped touchdown that traded three instead of seven for the Ravens. Then a fumble that was recovered for a touchdown by Atlanta. Then a dropped two-point conversion in the third quarter.

Andrews did manage to make some pivotal catches on the last drive in regulation that led to the tie and the overtime drive for the game-winner. But the Ravens could have won this in regulation if not for his mistakes. Still, Baltimore's offense is stuck with Andrews after Durham Smythe's injury. They simply don't have a choice. He's the most experienced tight end with only two rookies and Nick Vannett joining him on the active roster in an unfamiliar scheme. He needs to transition into being a possession tight end and stop trying to be the player he once was.

articles.title: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
articles.summary: The Steelers will play four of their next five games away from Acrisure Stadium. A trip to Paris to face the Saints will be the highlight.
articles.body:
The banged up Pittsburgh Steelers are about to start logging some heavy miles on top of their rough injury luck.

First-year coach Mike McCarthy's team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule.

All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently.

The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise's history and could determine whether the Steelers ' 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn't won an NFL playoff game since 2017.

NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That's a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes.

One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France.

How have Pittsburgh Steelers head coaches fared through the years?

It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date.

The Steelers got to enjoy a bye after their trip to the Emerald Isle and did not need to travel any further than Massachusetts until they visited the Los Angeles Chargers in early November. It was a similar story when they played in London13 years ago. They came home to a bye, and most travel was relatively local for the month before and after.

This time around, they'll have to turn around and face Cleveland at home the following Sunday before finally reaching the open date in the schedule.

Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight.

Along the way, McCarthy and GM Omar Khan will hope to get healthier and avoid further attrition.

The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards.

The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game.

That piles a heavy burden onto DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard as well as practice squad options Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson unless outside additions are made.

The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed.

McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence.

One notable addition to the injury report was defensive lineman Keeanu Benton. He missed practice Wednesday with an ankle injury, so that will be a new one to monitor throughout the week as his team prepares to hit the road.
